chapter_title: The Catechumen asks the Apostle: will Rest come ab
spiritual_reading:
When a person turns in full trust toward the good of love and asks for it, that asking is already joined to a genuine willing of what is asked; and because the Divine is compassion itself, such a turning opens reception. If the person’s turning is chiefly for the person’s own restoration, it is received according to that need; and if it is chiefly for another’s restoration, it is likewise received, because love looks beyond self and therefore more fully accords with heaven.

This form of asking is not new. From the first rising of ordered life, those who were first in spiritual intelligence turned themselves toward the Divine Source and sought aid; and what they sought was given, because the turning itself was an opening to influx.

I will describe how such asking is effected from the most ancient states; and in what manner the mind is formed to receive what it seeks, when it seeks the ordering of all things in itself.

The primary wisdom that proceeds from Divine love turned itself wholly to the First Divine, and from affection acknowledged, celebrated, and ascribed all power and all good to that Source. From this state of humility and love it sought a restoring influx; and it sought also a determinate provision of aid. And it received an ample communication of strength, together with the manifold operative faculties that attend wisdom when it is conjoined to love.

That same wisdom sought help on behalf of the primal good in a person, because that good had gone forth into ultimates and had immersed itself, and so had come into separation from its own higher life. It had relinquished itself into distress, and had entered combat in the lowest degree where destruction, grief, and weakening prevail—within the states of falsity and evil, within the deepest fears, amid the compulsions and cravings of hellish persuasions.

For it was as an inmost governing good beset by contrary forces on every side. Therefore that wisdom, in its turning to the First Divine, sought that a protecting and rescuing power might be sent—an aid for the Divine good now held in distress.

Accordingly the turning and intercession were received into the Divine presence; and the Divine provided what was sought: a great rescuing influx, the living operation of Divine truth that brings relief. Then wisdom and that living operation advanced in power to the outmost limits of the spiritual domain, and from there raised the embattled good out of the struggle in which it had been held.

That good, having been delivered, returned as a gift to wisdom; yet it had been made remote, because opposing forces had pressed it into severe distress and had weakened it in states devoid of good.

But the living operation of Divine truth took hold of it, liberated it, restored it to order, and gave it tranquility in a state of peace and protection. This relief was according to the united intention of the three—of Divine love, of wisdom from love, and of living truth in act—so that what is received might be welcomed and remain conjoined.

Thus a beloved power was brought near again: the primal good that had been far off and fixed in distress. The rescuing operation entered the state of devastation and weakness, and by redeeming action released it from affliction, established it in rest and joy, and made its peace enduring.

This is the first ancient turning by which wisdom sought aid; and the aid was granted.

After this, the ordered arrangement of the spiritual and natural degrees was established and brought to completion: the higher and lower structures of reception were arranged; the recurring orderly motions of life were set in place; the conveyances of living intelligence in elevated states were provided; the bonds that hold order together were fixed; the external planes of life with their boundaries and defenses were formed; and containing forms were prepared for uses. Thus the whole was made coherent and set into right order by the Divine goods and truths that proceed from the heavenly source.

Then the primary wisdom stood together with the beloved illumination, with the forming power that orders, with the living operation of Divine truth, and with the primal good now restored. These five entered a state of prayerful turning; they acknowledged and celebrated the First Divine, and sought an additional provision: that there might be given to them a leading and guiding power for all the uses they had now formed, and that this power might come to purify the living soul still held in distress.

Their turning was received, and what they sought was given. A new saving presence was called forth: a third proceeding that acts as manifest mediation. This proceeding came in the might of Divine greatness and surveyed the whole living soul—how it was bound by compulsions and held fast. It perceived the ordered works that the other saving powers had established from higher states; and again it perceived the living soul still chained in grievous torment, oppressed by the foul delight of the deepest falsity conjoined with it.

Therefore this mediating proceeding, from love, made its mode of salvation plain before the deepest hellish state, in order to free the living soul. It redeemed it from the deadened cravings and corporeal lusts in which it suffered, brought relief, and restored it into a state of rest and joy.

And this saving mediation also fulfilled the united intention of the three—according to the desire of the companion powers who had sought the Divine for it. Thus what had been asked was granted in a form suited to effect deliverance.

The third work was the removal and elevation of the living soul that had been freed: it was released from bondage, relieved of affliction, and set into a governing order, becoming primary with respect to the whole formed life of the person.

Thus you have been instructed in the second ancient turning by which they sought the Divine; and the mediating saving presence was given.

A third turning followed, but its record here is broken and does not yield a fully continuous account. Still, the fragment indicates a further revelation of Divine manifestation and a concealment from those not prepared; a standing firm of what is Divine; an unveiling of truth as light; a renewal of the primal good; a contempt or mockery from opposites; an exalted state presented; an investing with outward truth; a liberation of those held; a raising of confession; and a return to prayer and asking for release—together with the mediating saving power.

What remains suggests that the living are conjoined in permanence; that a first saving act is effected out of what is opposed; and that hope is given.

Also, a more interior Divine manifestation perfected the intention of salvation, so that the light was found and the will was brought into agreement with what is heavenly. And the Divine granted a further power of illumination and rescue—an appearing of Divine truth in splendor—by which the demands of the lowest states were answered in order, and hope was secured. This manifestation was made low so that it could reach those held in opposition; and its quality was displayed even to enemies. Thus hope was received, and the light-bearing power was revealed as the granted entreaty of the beings of light.

And as this turning took that form, so too the mind is to be set into a similar form, made stable by an image of order received within. For everyone who knows and perceives in themselves the things that flow in from a higher source—and how they are received and arranged—has within an exemplar by which stability is given.

The first and chief effect of this saving manifestation is the liberation of the living soul that is entangled and bound throughout the whole ordered system of life; for by means of this Divine operation it is to be freed, cleansed, purified, and redeemed.

It redeems the living person who is held fast in every way, because it proceeds from the First Divine and carries Divine pity as living power. By it redemption is made for the soul that is freed; and the way of salvation is opened. Therefore the Divine is asked again that relief may be granted in affliction, and that what is sought may be given. It is sought for the soul that has come forth out of the world of bondage, that it may be set into peace, freed from distress, and brought forth into enduring life.

And the living soul that is freed through the aid of another soul is likewise redeemed in the name and quality of that person. It is purified and restored to its first essence, and then becomes a fellow-helper. From that new state it also seeks aid for the soul of the one who has been released from the external self; it asks love and forgiveness from the powers of light—that is, it desires conjunction with good and the removal of evils by heavenly truths.

And as relief has been given to the living soul by means of this cooperation, so the cooperating soul also finds relief and is delivered from the external bonds that held it. It is elevated into the state of light; and because a soul was redeemed through it, salvation is effected for it as well; and it comes into the state of life and rest that endures.

fills.notes: The substrate logic requires continuity: this entreaty is primordial, beginning with the first ordered beings turning to the Source. The phrase links “since the beginning” with “the gods first made entreaty”.
In the spiritual translation, the asking concerns “the ordering of all things in itself.” This fill supplies the object of the request and keeps the impersonal, structural register.

fills.fill: by the will of the Father and the Mother and the Living Spirit.
fills.notes: The passage explicitly speaks of “the will of these three” in the spiritual sense: Divine love, wisdom-from-love, and living truth-in-act. In the oldest-layer vocabulary this is Father, Mother of Life, Living Spirit.

The sequence needs the technical cosmological role that makes reception and conjunction possible (“welcomer… find with the welcomer”). In the oldest substrate this is a light-being function, not ecclesial language.

fills.fill: the living soul that is brought up from the war may remain in its place of rest.
fills.notes: The broken sentence is about what is ‘found with’ the Welcomer: a stabilized reception so the rescued principle remains conjoined in rest, matching the correspondential explanation of welcoming and remaining.

fills.fill: And then she brought near again
fills.notes: The fragment resumes the narrative-result of the first entreaty: the previously distant beloved power is brought near again.
Old-layer myth regularly expresses restoration as reinvestment or clothing (a correspondence for re-formation in truths). It also anticipates the later broken ‘garment’ motif in ¶25.
Keeps the clause coherent: “a great power … of the loved one …” The loved one is the restored First Man; what is described is the rescuing power operative in him.

The construction of the ordered universe (firmaments, wheels, ships, fastenings, walls, vessels) presupposes deliberative ordering by the light-powers; this is the impersonal, cosmogonic transition expected here.
They ask for “the power … the leader, a guide… That he might come and purify the living soul.” Thus the missing apposition identifies the power as purifier as well as leader and guide.
Connects “he received from them their prayer” with the consequent gift; required by English syntax.
Balances the parallelism “he gave them their entreaty and their request … he summoned…”
The Father ‘summons from himself’ the mediating saving presence; in the substrate this is called forth as a ‘great power’ before being named the Third Ambassador.
The Ambassador acts ‘in his charity’; correspondentially this is compassion as an operative motive of rescue. The verb is required to complete the clause.
“together with the … of the Father” must be an impersonal divine act that effects the granting: a command or decree. ‘Command’ suits the oldest-layer cosmological tone.
The clause needs the Father’s receptive act before “he gave the entreaty.” ‘Hearkened’ keeps the archaic, impersonal register and matches the ‘received their prayer’ motif.
The third entreaty, in Manichaean sequence, is tied to the Third Ambassador’s revelatory display that draws forth the soul; the fragment’s “displayed his image” aligns to him.
Minimal connective demanded by the broken parataxis.
The ‘image’ is hidden from those not prepared: correspondentially the hellish governors. Old-layer term: rulers, not moralized language.

fills.fill: in the midst of the heights;
fills.notes: “he stood firm” needs a location/state of stability; ‘heights’ correspond to the higher degree where the divine stands unshaken.
Paratactic link.
Balances “he hid his image” with a contrary act: revealing to those who can receive; required by the spiritual translation’s ‘unveiling’.
Completes “they revealed … the light …” with the recipient implied; minimal syntactic repair.
Old substrate often treats the revealed ‘light’ here as a noetic manifestation that orders and draws up the soul. ‘Mind’ fits the correspondential ‘image’ and ‘figure’ motifs used later in ¶28.
The fragment includes “the First Man … mock …”; the turning-point is recollection/recognition of the First Man as archetypal good in ultimates, preceding opposition’s mockery.
Mockery is attributed to opposites; in this myth those are demons and rulers of Darkness.
Needs a collective subject for mockery and shouting; ‘assembly’ preserves impersonal cosmological style.
“which is exalted” most naturally qualifies a ‘place’ or ‘region’ of height corresponding to an elevated state.
Exalted place is characterized by ‘glory’ in the light-register without importing later devotional tone.
Modifies ‘garment’ to express correspondence: outward truth investing the saved as luminous form.
Completes the common collocation “garment of light,” a standard substrate motif for investiture in truths.
Paratactic link.
Those ‘freed’ in this context are the living soul-principles being extracted from bondage.
Gives motion toward the revealer after freeing; matches spiritual sense: raising and return to confession.
Pairs with ‘their voice’ as confession; keeps cosmological liturgical action without church overlay.
Required preposition before “the body”.
Possessive for “body,” referring to those praying from within embodiment.
Matches “prayer … it … beseech …” as a renewed act of asking after revelation.
Fills verbal noun consistent with the repeated ‘beseech’ sequence.
Minimal connective for the object of beseeching.
The spiritual translation explicitly ends the fragment with “asking for release—together with the mediating saving power.”
The fragment’s spiritual sense: the living are conjoined in permanence. ‘He joined them’ states the conjunction effected by the saving power.
Those conjoined ‘for ever’ are the living ones who have been freed; keeps the substrate term ‘redeemed’ as cosmological extraction, not moral preaching.
Adds the state-character of the conjunction (rest, stability), matching repeated ‘place of rest and joy’.
“the first … from the …” needs a noun of operation; ‘saving act’ is neutral, structural.
The spiritual translation: ‘effected out of what is opposed’. Old-layer term: opposites (powers of darkness).
Completes “he gave him the hope …” with enduring character of hope.
Jesus the Splendour ‘perfected the will’ in alignment with the Divine Source; ‘of the Father’ supplies the governing referent in oldest-layer terms.
The will is also ‘of the lights’ as the collective of light-powers aligned to the Father; fits the cosmological register.
“they found the light …” is for the living soul held in the mixture; naming it stabilizes the referent in the broken line.
The text already mentions “will of the elements”; this earlier lacuna likely introduces them as the lower constituents needing ordering.
“that he had … he gave them the power” needs a past participle: he had ordered or arranged the elements, matching correspondential ‘ordering’.
Balances ‘ordered’ with fixation into stable forms; corresponds to ‘set firm’ motif.
Prepares “for ever”; shows permanence of the ordering.
“This first … he was humbled” needs identification: a saving power that can descend. Keeps impersonal cosmology.
Connective for the descent motif.
He was ‘made free’ from bonds; corresponds to liberation from compulsion and chains.
“the ...-ness is displayed to his enemies” calls for an abstract quality; ‘likeness’ fits the display of an image-form even to enemies.
Completes the display-action and links to “He received the hope”.
Hope is received by the bound soul; keeps cosmological focus.
Completes “the entreaty of the … of light” as ‘beings of light’, matching the spiritual translation.
“just as this entreaty …” needs completion: it was fulfilled in a particular form.
Pairs with “the figure” as “took the figure,” matching the spiritual translation.
The spiritual sense: stability by an image of order received within. This supplies the interior reception.
Applies the cosmological pattern to the formation of mind without preaching; describes analogical formation.
Interiorization is essential to correspondence: the image within gives firmness.
Directly corresponds to the spiritual translation’s ‘image of order’.
Connective.
Instrument of being set firm.
The ‘you are set firm’ is in the mental form, matching the spiritual translation’s focus.
Begins the relative clause “Every one … knows”.
Connective between knows and has perceived.
Supplies the verb for “all the things … out from … within him … upon him”: influx is the theme; ‘flow’ matches correspondential influx.
The spiritual translation: “The first and chief effect … is the liberation.” In substrate diction: redemption as extraction and purification of the living soul.
He redeems the living person entangled ‘in the body’—the natural ultimate where bonds are felt.
“He has … his father” needs a verb of procession; correspondentially all saving power proceeds from the First Source.
Fixes the title already used: the Father as ‘first established one’.
Connective in the chain of statements.
Redemption is ‘by the power’ of the saving manifestation; keeps impersonal causality.
Matches spiritual translation: ‘the way of salvation is opened’.
Leads into repeated asking; keeps the impersonal “they” of the light-powers.
Connects ‘request’ with ‘affliction’: they ask for relief for the soul in affliction.
Marks the renewed parallel petition.
Completes “just as he has … of the light”.
“of the light” modifies ‘powers’ in this mythology.
Introduces purpose clause “give ease… grant…”.
“give ease for his …” refers to his companion powers as brothers (as in ¶19).
Completes “grant the entreaty and the request” with indirect object.

fills.fill: and bring it forth into the land of light
fills.notes: The closing movement is extraction from the world into the light-realm, matching the spiritual translation’s “brought forth into enduring life.” Old-layer place-name: land of light.
Connects “It goes into the land of light” with the clause about the redeemed soul.
The spiritual translation: “because a soul was redeemed through it, salvation is effected for it as well.” This provides the noun of effect.
Closes with the enduring state of life and rest; matches chapter’s repeated ‘for ever’.

assessment: Much of the chapter’s early section (¶6–¶23) is tightly constrained by the standard cosmogonic sequence (Mother of Life → Living Spirit → Third Ambassador) and by the correspondential roles named in the spiritual translation, so restorations there are mostly moderate-to-strong. The long broken record of the third entreaty (¶25–¶28) is only loosely constrained; fills there are necessarily more conjectural and were kept generic, structural, and in oldest-layer cosmological diction (image, light, garment of light, rulers, bonds, order). The final doctrinal applications (¶31, ¶37, ¶44) are again fairly constrained by the stated spiritual outcomes (redemption, opening of the way, relief in affliction, elevation to land of light).
